name: Geographic Pattern Capillary Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Capillary Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, geographic-shaped erythematous to violaceous capillary malformation on the skin
Congenital or early infancy onset of the vascular lesion
Lack of visible telangiectasia within the lesion differentiating from other vascular anomalies
Lesion distribution following a geographic or map-like pattern rather than linear or segmental

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital geographic-shaped capillary malformation with characteristic lesion morphology and distribution pattern
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; biopsy and imaging are rarely required unless associated syndromic features are suspected.

searchTerms: red skin patch with map-like shape

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital onset of vascular skin lesion
searchTerms: vascular skin lesion present from birth

common.symptomName: Progressive darkening or hypertrophy of affected skin
searchTerms: skin getting darker and thicker over time

common.symptomName: Soft tissue hypertrophy underlying the lesion

searchTerms: face affected on one side only

common.symptomName: Mild localized edema in affected area
searchTerms: mild swelling in affected skin area

eye problems like increased eye pressure
ocular issues linked to vascular lesions

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to associated syndromes
occasional.notes: Present only if part of syndromic association
searchTerms: brain or nerve problems from associated conditions

occasional.symptomName: Localized pain or discomfort in lesion area
searchTerms: pain or discomfort in lesion area

rare.symptomName: Development of pyogenic granuloma within lesion
searchTerms: growth of red, bleeding skin bump within lesion

rare.symptomName: Syndromic associations with Sturge-Weber syndrome features
searchTerms: syndrome with vascular birthmark and neurological signs
complex syndrome involving skin and brain

imaging: MRI or CT to evaluate underlying soft tissue or brain involvement if syndromic features suspected
Doppler ultrasound to assess blood flow within lesion
genetic: Somatic mutations in GNAQ gene identified in affected tissue
other: Clinical examination remains primary diagnostic tool

distinguishingFeatures: Typically linear or segmental distribution rather than geographic
May have associated neurological or ocular involvement in syndromic cases
Less likely to have geographic pattern

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth or nodularity suggesting pyogenic granuloma
Neurological symptoms indicating possible Sturge-Weber syndrome
Ocular hypertension or glaucoma in ipsilateral eye
